item.title: Arbol Names Chief Scientist, Launches Innovation Unit
item.description: (Image source: Arbol homepage.) Arbol (New York), a vertically integrated insurance organization, has appointed Clement Atzberger Chief Scientist and launched an Innovation Unit under his direction. Clement Atzberger Chief Scientist, Arbol. The unit will develop modeling, data and underwriting research intended to support Arbol’s specialty risk business and expand the range of risks its insurance operations can price and write.

item.title: Tinubu Adds Conversational Configuration to Skye
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Tinubu (Paris) has introduced conversational configuration in Tinubu Skye v11, allowing specialty insurance business teams to describe application requirements in plain language and have the platform generate configurations for expert review before production. “With conversational configuration in Tinubu Skye v11, the people who understand the risk describe the change they need and the platform configures it, without starting a project every time.” From Intent to Governed Configuration Tinubu Skye is designed for specialty insurance applications across underwriting intake, distribution, policy administration and claims. Internally, having Tinubu as a partner is an experience that surprises us with every launch and every evolution of the platform.” Conversational configuration is generally available to customers running Tinubu Skye v11, with additional capabilities planned through the fourth quarter of 2026.

item.title: Weather Damage Turning into Long-term Debt for Homeowners: Report
item.description: “When a single weather event can push homeowners into years of debt, the damage extends far beyond the property. Nearly 25% of homeowners who paid out of pocket for weather damage are still carrying debt from it. homeowners paid out of pocket for weather damage in the past three years and only 22% feel very financially prepared for an unexpected weather repair, according to tech-native insurance group Hippo Holdings.

item.title: CatIQ lifts Ontario & Quebec thunderstorm insured market loss estimate 12% to C$491m
item.description: CatIQ, Canada’s insured loss and exposure index provider, has raised its insurance industry loss estimate for the severe thunderstorm event that impacted parts of southern Ontario and southern Quebec between June 30th and July 3rd, 2026, to CAD $491 million, a 12% increase from the firm’s second loss estimate of $439 million. CatIQ also confirmed that it will publish an updated loss estimate for the severe thunderstorm event on January 5th, 2027. CatIQ published its initial loss estimate from the event back in early August, putting the total at the time at $374 million.

item.title: US title insurance premiums rise 13% in 2025 as growth continues, reports AM Best
item.description: AM Best, the credit rating agency and provider of insurance industry research and analysis, has reported continued growth in the US title insurance market, with premiums increasing by 13% in 2025 and further gains recorded during the opening quarter of 2026. AM Best said its composite of title insurers recorded an 18% increase in direct premiums written in the first quarter of 2026 compared with the corresponding period in 2025. “With interest rates likely to remain higher for longer, activity on the residential side will likely be limited and leave the possibility for title insurance premium growth to be tied squarely to the commercial real estate market.” Financial performance across the title insurance segment also improved during 2025.

item.title: Markel International raises London Fine Art & Specie capacity to $250m
item.description: Markel Insurance, the insurance operation within Markel Group Inc., has raised its London Fine Art & Specie capacity from USD 100 million to USD 250 million through Lloyd’s of London to accommodate rising demand. Danny O’Donoghue, Head of Fine Art & Specie, Markel International, commented, “Clients are increasingly requiring larger limits due to rising valuations of fine art collections, significant increases in precious metals values and greater concentrations of high-value assets. The move also strengthens Markel’s ability to support larger and more complex Fine Art & Specie risks.

item.title: Pacific Life Re completes $3bn longevity reinsurance agreement with American National
item.description: Pacific Life Re, the global reinsurance business of Pacific Life, has announced the successful execution of a $3 billion longevity reinsurance agreement with American National Insurance Company. Adding: “This transaction highlights our ability to deliver tailored longevity solutions at scale and demonstrates our strong commitment to support PRT markets and policyholders worldwide.” Howie Timothy, AVP Client Solutions, North America, Savings & Retirement, Pacific Life Re, stated: “We are very proud to have partnered closely with American National on this deal and to showcase our capabilities and expertise in a new market. We look forward to continued partnership with the team at American National.” Pacific Life Re were supported on the deal by global law firm Eversheds Sutherland.

item.title: Data Centers Pump $340M Into Rural Texas Projects
item.description: As data centers move into the state at a rapid pace, Texas communities in mostly rural areas face a fiscal cliff from property tax cuts, inflation and overall economic uncertainty. These are just some of the public investments data center companies have paid for across rural Texas in the past year. The Texas Tribune reviewed news releases, public meeting agendas and interviewed local officials to understand how data centers are using their money in Texas.

item.title: Missouri AG Secures $42K Judgment Against Contractor Accused of Fraud
item.description: Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway announced that her office secured a jury conviction against Daniel Eschliman for scamming an elderly couple out of more than $42,000. Eschliman was criminally charged in one other contractor fraud case and has been sued civilly numerous times. The case was investigated by the Attorney General’s Office’s Consumer Protection Section after the victims filed a complaint against Eschliman.

item.title: Thousands of European Wind, Solar Power Systems Exposed Online: Dutch Researchers
item.description: Thousands of administrative systems at wind and solar power parks in Europe are exposed to the internet, potentially giving attackers access to interfaces that can stop turbines and raising the risk of sabotage, Dutch researchers warned on Tuesday . “If you can turn off the energy within the city or the airport, imagine that at a larger scale.” Using machine learning to sort and cluster data, the pair said they identified 8,547 internet-facing systems they could link to at specific solar parks (7,942) and wind farms (605) in 35 European countries, which should not have been exposed to the internet. The exposed systems included administrative and login interfaces as well as operational interfaces showing data and controls.

item.title: Heffernan acquires Walterry Insurance Brokers
item.description: Heffernan Insurance has acquired Walterry Insurance Brokers, an independent agency based in Clinton, Maryland. The Walterry team joined Heffernan effective May 1, 2026. Founded in 1968, Walterry specializes in media liability, professional liability and business insurance, serving newspapers, broadcasters, film and television producers, and nonprofit trade associations.

item.title: Grinnell files trademark application for “Farmutual”
item.description: Grinnell Mutual has filed a trademark application for “Farmutual” covering tax consulting and filing, accounting, insurance claims adjustment, and insurance consulting and information services. Grinnell also previously used the FarMutual name in its member branding. Filed on October 1, 2026, the application has not yet been assigned to an examiner.

item.title: 2027 Insurance Trends: The Math is Getting More Complicated
item.description: Heading into 2027, some of the math is getting particularly complicated in ways we haven’t seen before. This ultimately makes some of the less flashy changes happening across insurance more important than ever. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety notes that vehicles equipped with crash-avoidance sensors can cost more to repair after comparable crashes because sensors themselves are expensive and often require calibration after replacement.

item.title: Trump Names Intelligence Chief Clayton as AI Czar, to Head Task Force
item.description: Trump, who has pushed to rename artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” said Clayton would head the newly created Super Intelligence Force (SIF), overseeing the government’s engagement with consumers, religious groups, AI companies and other stakeholders. In addition to Clayton, the task force’s leaders will include Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor, Trump wrote. US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton the administration’s AI czar, tasking him with coordinating the federal government’s efforts to maintain US leadership in the technology.

item.description: data center market is expanding rapidly, driven by artificial intelligence, advanced encryption, cryptocurrency mining and other emerging technologies. Large and complex property rates with WTW’s portfolio dropped 14.5% in the second quarter of 2026, according to the fall 2026 edition of its Insurance Marketplace Realities report. The report examines dozens of lines of commercial business in North America.

item.title: Looking at how we interact with whistleblowers
item.description: I know the many colleagues who are in contact with whistleblowers and vulnerable individuals always aim to treat them as the people they are – with empathy and professionalism, not simply cases to be managed. To build greater confidence, we’re sharing more information with whistleblowers about the action we take. item.title: Crunchbase Data Shows AI’s Most Active Startups Are Becoming Serial Acquirers
item.description: Some of the AI industry’s fastest-growing startups are becoming serial acquirers, buying smaller companies to fill product gaps, enter new markets and bring specialized teams in-house, a review of Crunchbase data shows. The question we always ask is: does this deal get us somewhere faster than we’d get there ourselves?” Some of the AI acquirers have returned to the dealmaking table more than once in recent years, Crunchbase data shows. 29, according to Crunchbase data — 14% more than in all of 2025.

item.title: Third-party capital more than just complementary capacity for Hannover Re: Althoff
item.description: Sven Althoff, Member of the Executive Board for Property & Casualty at Hannover Re, has said that third-party capital is certainly part of the reinsurer’s strategy, describing it as more than just complementary capacity, whilst also adding that it is creating opportunities for Hannover Re. During the webinar, Althoff was asked whether he sees third-party capital as competition, complementary capacity or an integral part of Hannover Re’s own capital strategy. Althoff outlined that while third-party capital is a competitor in some respects, Hannover Re sees it as being more of a partner and opportunity to grow its business further.

item.title: Economics of ILS and appetites of investors change with the reinsurance cycle: Moody’s
item.description: In a recent report, Moody’s Ratings highlights how the economics of catastrophe bonds and insurance-linked securities change over time, driven by the softening global reinsurance market cycle. Moody’s Ratings recent report on the insurance-linked securities market, releases just in advance of the Monte Carlo Rendez-vous event, shows how cyclicality in reinsurance has played across into catastrophe bond pricing, with the agency saying this has changed the economics and as a result investor appetites are evolving. The last five years has shown the cycle remains fully in-force across reinsurance and whatever the unlock may be, that can make risk and capital flow more freely along the market chain and so moderate pricing cyclicality, has yet to be seen.

item.title: VisionFund teams with Global Parametrics on two-peril Amazon Basin parametric insurance
item.description: VisionFund, the financial inclusion arm of World Vision, working alongside with Global Parametrics and co-financed by the InsuResilience Solutions Fund, will design a two-peril parametric meso-insurance product for World Vision offices in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Peru, as part of the wider Amazon Basin Initiative. The firm’s explained that that the integrated approach builds on VisionFund’s experience in inclusive insurance, including more than eight years of climate meso-insurance, along with World Vision’s extensive disaster preparedness and response experience in the Amazon Basin region and globally. Solène Favre, VisionFund Global Director, Inclusive Insurance, commented: “This approach moves disaster and climate response from reactive fundraising towards pre-arranged, predictable protection.

item.title: Nikola Milutinović joins Newline Europe as Regional Underwriting Manager for Northern Germany
item.description: Newline Europe, a Cologne-based insurance company authorised by the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority, has appointed Nikola Milutinović as Regional Underwriting Manager for Northern Germany with effect from 1 October 2026. Newline Europe explained that this newly created role strengthens its presence in northern Germany and supports further growth in the region. Manuel Wirtz, CEO of Newline Europe, commented, “By establishing our own presence in northern Germany, we are taking an important step in the further development of Newline Europe.

item.title: Santam Syndicate 1918 appoints Sam Geddes as Active Underwriter
item.description: Santam Syndicate 1918, part of Santam Group, Africa’s non-life insurer, has announced that Sam Geddes will assume the responsibilities of Active Underwriter. According to Santam Syndicate 1918, the appointment comes as the Syndicate continues to develop its underwriting platform and expand its presence in the Lloyd’s market. Santam Syndicate 1918 has also announced the promotion of Sam Tierney and Briyangha (Brie) Suthagaran from Assistant Underwriters to Underwriters within its Property D&F team.

item.title: Aon reinforces commitment to Taiwan with new corporate office in Taipei
item.description: Aon, a global professional services firm specialising in risk, insurance, retirement and health solutions, has announced the relocation of its Taiwan corporate office at Fubon A25 in Xinyi District. It reflects our long-term commitment to Taiwan and creates an environment for our colleagues to collaborate, innovate and succeed, while continuing to deliver the insights and solutions our clients need in an increasingly complex risk environment.” Designed to support a modern working style, the new office includes dedicated spaces for focused work, collaboration and team meetings, fostering greater connectivity among colleagues within a custom-built environment. Lee Huang Ng, Chairperson and CEO of Taiwan, Aon, commented: “The opening of our new office in Xinyi District is an important milestone for our Taiwan business.

item.title: L’Oreal Explores Unloading Chemical-Related Liabilities, WSJ Reports
item.description: L’Oreal has engaged restructuring advisers to explore options for rising US legal liabilities linked to its use of talc and other chemical ingredients in some of its cosmetic products, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday. The Journal said L’Oreal is considering moving tort liabilities into a separate corporate entity to unload them through a sale to an outside investor, allowing the company to separate its exposure from its operating businesses. As an option to address the claims outside Chapter 11, L’Oreal’s advisers are exploring a sale similar to Honeywell’s divestiture last year of certain asbestos liabilities to corporate liability acquisition platform Delticus, the Journal said.

item.title: Rubio Asks Russia to Share More Information About Plague Death
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that Russia should share more information about the death of a plague laboratory worker who died last week, an incident which he said Washington was watching “very closely.” “I think it’s incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world,” Rubio told reporters in Iceland. Rubio said the US has “measures” available to help Russia if the situation turns out to be more serious than has so far been acknowledged, but needed to know more before it could step in. (Editor’s note: The plague research institute is located in Irkutsk, a city in the Siberian Federal District of eastern Russia.) Russian authorities have said the situation is under control.

item.title: New York Declares US Measles Disaster Emergency
item.description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on Monday over a measles outbreak, the first such declaration by a U.S. New York has reported 108 measles cases this year through October 3, including 92 since July 15 in under-immunized rural communities across 18 counties, well above typical annual levels, according to the executive order. The state also expanded the pool of health professionals allowed to administer measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccines as cases rise in rural communities.

item.title: Canopius replaces QBE as Castle Insurance underwriter
item.description: Castle Insurance, part of Australia’s Sure Insurance , has named Canopius as its new underwriter, replacing QBE Insurance Australia effective December 1, 2026. Castle offers home and contents insurance through brokers and has been operating for approximately 12 months. Sure Insurance Managing Director Bradley Heath said the partnership offers new growth opportunities for Castle, citing the companies’ shared focus on long-term partnerships and specialized risk selection.

item.title: Nettle raises $4.8 million
item.description: Nettle , an AI loss control platform for commercial insurers, has raised $4.8 million in seed funding led by MTech Capital, with participation from Project A, Sure Valley Ventures, Portfolio Ventures, and Ventures Together. The round brings its total funding to $6.8 million, following a $2 million pre-seed round in March 2025. Founded in 2024 by former McKinsey QuantumBlack colleagues Jack Miller and Katya Kinane, Nettle combines remote risk identification, guided inspections, evidence analysis, and report generation.

item.title: Saga to launch pet insurance product
item.description: Saga, the UK-based company offering products and services to people over 50, is launching a new pet insurance product. “We’re delighted to be bringing a bespoke pet insurance proposition to the market for Saga customers. By combining Allianz’s insurance expertise with Saga’s deep customer understanding, we’ve created something that feels relevant, accessible and genuinely unique for this audience.” – Isabella Von Mesterhazy, Managing Director of Allianz Specialty.

item.title: México alista nuevas reglas para pagos digitales: industria las apoya, pero pide preservar incentivos
item.description: La industria respalda el impulso a la digitalización, pero pide que las nuevas normas preserven la neutralidad tecnológica y mantengan incentivos para seguir expandiendo la aceptación de pagos electrónicos. México emprenderá reformas regulatorias para ampliar la aceptación de pagos digitales, con el objetivo de reducir costos para los comercios, extender el uso de medios electrónicos en trámites y servicios públicos y fortalecer la interoperabilidad entre bancos, fintechs y procesadores. Los cambios normativos avanzan en dos frentes: un anteproyecto regulatorio que plantea ajustes a los costos de procesamiento y a las cuotas de intercambio en operaciones con tarjeta, y la iniciativa de Ley de Economía Digital , que busca ampliar la aceptación de pagos electrónicos en los tres niveles de gobierno y facilitar una mayor adopción de códigos QR.

item.title: F&G files trademark application for “F&G FastPath”
item.description: F&G has filed a trademark application for “F&G FastPath” covering life insurance and annuity services. Filed on October 1, 2026, the application lists annuity underwriting, life insurance underwriting, issuance and administration of annuities, and issuance of life insurance. The application has not yet been assigned to an examiner.

item.title: Blitzy launches review tool for AI-generated code
item.description: Blitzy , an autonomous software development platform backed by Erie Strategic Ventures, Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures, and New York Life Ventures, has launched PR Review, a feature designed to help engineering teams understand and review AI-generated code faster. The launch addresses a growing bottleneck as AI agents generate code faster than engineers can review it. Blitzy’s process allows engineers to approve the proposed scope and approach before code generation, with automated tests, builds, benchmarks, and static analysis incorporated into development.

item.title: SIAA acquires Canopy Specialty Insurance
item.description: SIAA has acquired Canopy Specialty Insurance, a specialty commercial property and casualty MGA operating in the US and UK. The acquisition adds specialty underwriting and product development capabilities alongside SIAA’s agency alliance, retail business Sequel Insurance Agencies and wholesale operation Xchange. Canopy develops and underwrites niche commercial insurance products for small and midsized businesses, including contractors’ liability, excess casualty and legal indemnity programs.

item.title: Sedgwick: Property Claims Face Delays, Are Growing More Complex
item.description: Despite the promise of artificial intelligence and other technology to improve and speed the insurance process, property claims face delays and growing complexity, according to a new report that also shows claims costs are under pressure. Several factors are putting pressure on property claim timelines, including labor shortages, equipment delays and increasingly complex losses, according to Sedgwick’s annual Loss Adjusting Insights report . “It’s just what we call the silver tsunami and that’s really just kind of a moment, where we’re getting a little bit of a brain drain and claims are becoming more and more complex, just because of the intricacies of the policies the way they’re underwritten,” McCallum said.

item.title: Crunchbase Data: Q3 2026 Posted A Record Count Of Billion-Dollar Rounds As The Global AI Race Heats Up
item.description: Global venture funding totaled $159 billion in Q3 2026 with close to 6,000 startups funded, Crunchbase data shows. Funding to private companies has skyrocketed this year, totaling $679 billion in venture funding globally in Q1 through Q3 2026, per Crunchbase data. A notable shift in 2026 has been the number of startups that have raised billion-dollar-plus rounds.
